The halls boast of fully equipped modern conferencing facilities with a team of experienced chefs to prepare creative and customised delectable dishes for the palate.” Advertisement [Shahzad Aslam](https://hospitality.economictimes.indiatimes.com/tag/shahzad+aslam), head of sales, Leisure Hotels Group further added, “Located just off [Pari Chowk](https://hospitality.economictimes.indiatimes.com/tag/pari+chowk), this event facility in Greater Noida is a preferred venue to plan conferences, meetings, weddings, product launches or shows. Aditya Virvani, COO at the Embassy Group felt that hospitality complexes like the one inaugurated at the Embassy Manyata Business Park in Bengaluru were a tremendous value addition to the project.

](https://etimg.etb2bimg.com/photo/91279475.cms?mod=131856)Aditya Virvani, COO at the Embassy Group felt that hospitality complexes like the one inaugurated at the Embassy Manyata Business Park in Bengaluru were a tremendous value addition to the project. The launch of the massive 619-key [Hilton](https://hospitality.economictimes.indiatimes.com/tag/hilton) complex at the Manyata Business Park in Bengaluru was an opportunity to speak to Aditya Virwani, COO at the [Embassy Group](https://hospitality.economictimes.indiatimes.com/tag/embassy+group) about his company’s involvement in the hospitality sector. “Our approach has been pretty consistent—it is to have hospitality within the larger ecosystem, as a value add to the rest of the park. We had actually built the Hilton at [Embassy Golf Links](https://hospitality.economictimes.indiatimes.com/tag/embassy+golf+links) originally as a service apartment and had then converted it by doing a deal with Hilton,” said Virwani, speaking exclusively to ET HospitalityWorld. He went on to speak of the learnings the company had with their foray into hospitality in how to optimise the value and actually make sense on a yield on cost. The same learnings from their project at [Embassy](https://hospitality.economictimes.indiatimes.com/tag/embassy) Golf Links are reflected at the Manyata Park complex ranging from having a sub-brand with the Hilton Garden Inn, so that they didn’t lose out on business to the room sizes to having a large convention centre which was also an important revenue generator. From a builder’s point of view, Virwani felt that with the increase in input costs, it has become even more non-viable to build hotels—but the situation would allow existing properties to increase their rates. As we reflect on our past ceremonies, which have recognized the exceptional individuals and milestones shaping the industry's trajectory.** \\ \\ - Wed, 28 Oct 2026\\ - Hyatt Regency, New Delhi\\ \\ ![Restaurants and Nightlife Awards 2026](https://img.etb2bimg.com/imgv2/width-120,height-120,resize_mode-2/files/data_file_1776855148273_21199.jpg)](https://hospitality.economictimes.indiatimes.com/restaurant-nightlife-awards) [Know More](https://hospitality.economictimes.indiatimes.com/restaurant-nightlife-awards) Embassy is also constructing a similar complex of a 500-key complex with a Hilton and a Hilton Garden Inn at Embassy Tech Village on Bengaluru’s outer ring road, he added. On why they chose Hilton, Virwani said, “We find them from the business angle, really well connected with our tenants. They add so much value, because (the tenants) are mostly MNCs, who come here. They (the [hotels](https://hospitality.economictimes.indiatimes.com/tag/hotels)) are very efficiently run, from an optimisation point. They have a self-generating marketing tool from the connects. And they're also very business-centric”. He added that they were also open to evaluating other operators would the need arise. “I think even though the costs have gone up, it still makes sense because of the value creation it has from the office parks rent going up. So it's very hard to do a ROI on that. If you look at the hotel by itself, then it completely wouldn't make sense. But if you look at the overall park and how your renewals are now generating a huge premium. With the city traffic, such a mess when people fly in, and they have a week's worth of work in that park, it's so much more convenient for the brain to just walk to your room and eventually go to bed. So I think it will always make sense for the Embassy because we're doing large scale office parks,” he said about his company’s involvement in hospitality. ## Most Read in Hotels - [The Oberoi Group announces recipients of The Oberoi Group Scholarship Program](https://hospitality.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/hotels/the-oberoi-group-announces-recipients-of-the-oberoi-group-scholarship-program/134990303?utm_source=most_read&utm_medium=newsDetails) -
